text: Russian and DNR forces attacked Mariupol from the first days of the full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Russia claimed on 1 March 2022 to have encircled Mariupol by land and sea.
ISW assessed Mariupol as fully encircled as of 2 March 2022.
The Ukrainian garrison of Mariupol numbered about 3,500 according to a Ukrainian estimate quoted by The Economist; Russia claimed more than 8,000.

text: About 14,000 Russian and DNR attackers faced the Mariupol garrison.

text: The Mariupol garrison included the Azov Regiment, the 36th Marine Brigade, National Guard brigades, border guards and police.

text: Russian forces followed the encirclement of Mariupol with a deliberate bombardment of civilian infrastructure.
Russian forces bombed the Mariupol maternity hospital on 9 March 2022.

text: Russian forces struck the Mariupol drama theatre on 16 March 2022.
At least 10,284 people were buried in mass graves in Mariupol, according to HRW.
Russian forces cut Mariupol in two from the centre to the coast on 10 April 2022.
The 36th Marine Brigade's pocket at the Illich steel works fell on 13 April 2022.
When the Illich pocket fell on 13 April 2022, part of the 36th Marine Brigade broke through to Azovstal and its commander was captured.
notes: OUTCOME; commander captured is Baraniuk per section 4

text: The port of Mariupol fell about 16 April 2022.
On 21 April 2022 Putin declared victory in Mariupol and ordered Azovstal blockaded rather than stormed.
The Azovstal defenders used the plant's Soviet-era tunnels and shelters.
Azovstal covers about 11 km² above about 24 km of tunnels.

text: Seven Ukrainian Mi-8 missions with 16 helicopters flew ammunition, Stingers, NLAWs, Starlink terminals and 72 Azov volunteers into Azovstal and brought out wounded.

text: Three Ukrainian helicopters were lost on the Mariupol air bridge.
notes: OUTCOME; counts differ across sources (see section 11)

text: UN/ICRC convoys took civilians out of Azovstal between 30 April and 7 May 2022.
Russian troops broke into the Azovstal plant on 4 May 2022.
On 16 May 2022 the Ukrainian General Staff declared that the Mariupol garrison had "fulfilled its combat mission" and ordered the commanders to save their men's lives.

text: By 20 May 2022 Russia claimed 2,439 Ukrainian defenders had left Azovstal and surrendered.
At least 50 prisoners, many of them from Azovstal, were killed in the Olenivka barracks explosion of 28–29 July 2022.
The Azovstal plant held until the ordered "evacuation" of 16–20 May 2022.
Sources count the defence of Azovstal as 82 days (Wikipedia) or 83 days (Time).
There was no relief and no breakout of the Mariupol garrison; Ukraine's own position was that a military unblocking was impossible.
notes: OUTCOME; claimant is Hromov per section 3 and 7

text: The Ukrainian General Staff claimed the Mariupol defence pinned "up to 17 BTGs (about 20,000 personnel)", which thwarted a quick Russian drive on Zaporizhzhia.

US officials said two Russian BTGs remained at Mariupol on 9 May 2022.
The win band for the chapter is to hold Azovstal until mid-May 2022 while keeping between 2 and about 12 Russian BTGs at Mariupol after the city falls.
notes: OUTCOME; design synthesis from US figures

text: Mariupol fell in stages: the Illich works on 13 April 2022, the port about 16 April, and Russia announced victory on 21 April.
About 101 civilians left Azovstal in the first UN/ICRC operation (29 April – 3 May 2022).
About 173 civilians came out in the second UN/ICRC Azovstal operation, arriving on 8 May 2022.
Azovstal was clear of civilians on 7 May 2022.
The Mariupol air bridge flew seven missions with 16 Mi-8s, carried 72 troops in and 64 wounded out, delivered about 30 t, and lost 3 helicopters.

observations.subject: Mi-8 helicopters (sorties) on the air bridge

text: Russia claims 2,439 prisoners from Azovstal.
Ukrainian officials later used "about 2,500" for the number of Azovstal defenders taken prisoner.
The ICRC had registered only "hundreds" of Azovstal prisoners by 20 May 2022.
The Russian full-scale invasion began on 24 February 2022, and Mariupol was shelled from the first day.
On 25 February 2022 an advance from DNR-held territory on Mariupol was repelled near Pavlopil.
On 25 February 2022 Russian forces made an amphibious landing about 70 km west of Mariupol.
Electricity, gas and internet in Mariupol were cut on 28 February 2022.
On 1 March 2022 Russia claimed to have encircled Mariupol by land and sea.
On 1 March 2022 the Ukrainian General Staff said attacks on Mariupol by the 8th Combined Arms Army and DNR forces had failed.

text: ISW assessed on 2 March 2022 that Mariupol was fully encircled and that Russian forces were deliberately striking civilian infrastructure to force its surrender.
HRW dates the siege of Mariupol from 2 March 2022.
On 4 March 2022 the 8th Combined Arms Army (likely the 150th Motor Rifle Division) and proxy forces concentrated for an assault on Mariupol.
Repeated ceasefire and evacuation-corridor attempts for Mariupol failed under shelling between 5 and 8 March 2022.
On 7 March 2022 Azov commander Denys Prokopenko made a video appeal for a no-fly zone.
Mariupol Maternity and Children's Hospital No. 3 was bombed on 9 March 2022.
On 9 March 2022 the Ukrainian General Staff reported up to 17 Russian BTGs deployed from Kherson to Rozivka, about 47 km northwest of Mariupol.

text: The first civilian car convoys got out of Mariupol on 14–15 March 2022: about 160 cars on 14 March and about 20,000 people in 4,000 vehicles on 15 March.
ISW assessed on 15 March 2022 that the encirclement of Mariupol was deep enough to prevent a breakout or relief, with daily Russian assaults from east and west.
Just after 10:00 on 16 March 2022 the Mariupol drama theatre was hit by two 500 kg bombs; "ДЕТИ" (children) had been painted on the square.

bombs that hit the drama theatre

text: Fighting reached the Azovstal area on 19 March 2022.
Denys Prokopenko and Volodymyr Baraniuk were made Heroes of Ukraine on 19 March 2022.
The first Mariupol air-bridge helicopter mission was scrubbed on 19 March 2022 and flew two days later.
On 20 March 2022 the Mariupol defenders rejected a Russian surrender ultimatum.
On 20 March 2022 Russia confirmed that Black Sea Fleet deputy commander Andrei Paly had been killed in Mariupol.
Between 03:30 and 07:30 on 21 March 2022, mission 1 of the Mariupol air bridge flew two Mi-8s from Dnipro, refuelled at the line and crossed 60 mi of occupied ground to Azovstal.
Mission 1 of the Mariupol air bridge on 21 March 2022 brought Stingers, NLAWs and Starlink to Azovstal and took out about 16 wounded.

On mission 2 of the Mariupol air bridge in late March 2022, a few days after mission 1, a Russian missile pierced one engine of a Mi-8 without exploding; the helicopter limped home with about 20 wounded.
notes: exact date not given ("a few days later")

text: Russian forces entered the Mariupol city centre on 24 March 2022.
Ukraine struck Russian landing ships in Berdiansk on 24 March 2022.

At dawn on 28 March 2022, mission 3 ("Vitaliy") of the Mariupol air bridge flew as two single-ship missions with guns removed for 200 kg of extra medicine, through fog on the coast, and spent 12 minutes on the ground.

text: On 28 March 2022 Russian forces took the Azov Regiment's headquarters and the Kalmiuskyi district administration in Mariupol.
The Mariupol mayor's office said on 28 March 2022 that about 5,000 people had been killed in the city.
Russian thermobaric munitions were filmed at Mariupol on 30 March 2022, and the 150th Motor Rifle Division was taking heavy losses.
On 31 March 2022 AP reported that a helicopter carrying a wounded evacuee from Mariupol was hit in one engine on the way out.
On 31 March 2022 Chinese TV showed a downed Ukrainian Mi-8 near Mariupol; its link to the air-bridge missions is unclear.
Russian forces captured the SBU headquarters in Mariupol on 2 April 2022, and the defenders were bisected or trisected.
ISW assessed on 4 April 2022 that the Mariupol defenders had "outperformed" its estimates.
Russia claimed on 4 April 2022 that 267 marines of the 503rd Battalion had been captured in Mariupol.
At about 02:00 on 5 April 2022, on the last air-bridge mission according to Serbov, reinforcements were flown into Azovstal and the helicopter was shot down on the way back.
On 5 April 2022 a rescue Mi-8 sent from Dnipro after the last air-bridge mission was downed by MANPADS.
Unconfirmed Telegram photos of 6–7 April 2022 showed a FAB-3000 beside a Tu-22M, allegedly for use against Azovstal.
On 8 April 2022 Ukrainian forces held the port in southwest Mariupol and Azovstal in the east.
Pro-Russian sources claimed on 8 April 2022 that 3,000 Ukrainian troops were in Azovstal.
On 10 April 2022 Russian forces bisected Mariupol from the centre to the coast and took the fishing port west of Azovstal.
On 11 April 2022 Ukraine made an unverified allegation that a chemical agent had been used against the Mariupol defenders.
On the night of 11–12 April 2022 the 36th Marine Brigade broke out of the Illich steel works.
In the Illich breakout of 11–12 April 2022, Baraniuk's group headed north and was captured, while Volynskyi led about 500 men to Azovstal.
The Illich steel works fell on 13 April 2022.
Russia claimed on 13 April 2022 that 1,026 marines had surrendered at Illich; ISW called this likely false.
Oleksii Arestovych confirmed on 13 April 2022 that the 36th Marine Brigade had linked up with Azov.
On 14 April 2022 Ukrainian officials admitted "some" marines were captured in the Illich breakout.
On 16 April 2022 DNR forces reached the beach and entered the base of the 12th National Guard Brigade in Mariupol.
Tu-22M bombers struck Azovstal on 16 April 2022.
The Mariupol mayor's adviser warned on 16 April 2022 of FAB-3000 use against the city.
ISW assessed that the Mariupol port was likely lost on 16–17 April 2022 and organised Ukrainian resistance was reduced to Azovstal.
Russia issued an ultimatum to the Azovstal defenders with a deadline of 06:00 Moscow time on 17 April 2022.
Serhii Volynskyi wrote a letter to Pope Francis on 18 April 2022.
On 19 April 2022 the DNR announced an assault on Azovstal, and the defenders refused another Russian surrender demand.
A Ukrainian marine officer claimed on 20 April 2022 that about 500 border guards and police had moved from the port to Azovstal.

observations.subject: border guards and police moved to Azovstal

text: On 21 April 2022 Putin and Shoigu declared victory in Mariupol; Putin halted the assaults and ordered a blockade of Azovstal.
US officials said a dozen Russian BTGs were still in Mariupol on 21 April 2022.
On 22 April 2022 the Russian MoD said there would be no humanitarian pause at Azovstal until "white flags" were raised, and claimed the plant would run out of supplies in two weeks.
Some Russian units left Mariupol for Donetsk without refit on 23 April 2022.
Russian ground attacks on Azovstal resumed on 25 April 2022.
On 27 April 2022 Volynskyi's "Dunkirk" video said there were more than 600 wounded at Azovstal.
On 27 April 2022 the Azovstal defenders were low on food, water and ammunition.
On 28 April 2022 the field hospital in Azovstal was reportedly hit by "bunker-buster" bombs from seven Tu-22s.
A UN/ICRC convoy left Zaporizhzhia for Azovstal, about 230 km away, on 29 April 2022.
The UN/ICRC convoy reached Azovstal on 30 April 2022 and civilians came out between 30 April and 2 May.
Russia called the civilians evacuated from Azovstal in early May 2022 "hostages".
The UN said on 3 May 2022 that 101 civilians had come out of Azovstal plus 58 from Manhush, and 127 had reached Zaporizhzhia.
Russian air, artillery and ground assaults on Azovstal resumed on 3 May 2022.
Sviatoslav Palamar said 2 civilians were killed at Azovstal on 3 May 2022.
On 4 May 2022 Russian forces entered the Azovstal plant itself for the first time, and communications with the defenders were lost.
On 6 May 2022, during the ceasefire, an ATGM hit a vehicle moving to evacuate civilians from Azovstal, killing 1 and wounding 6, according to Azov.
Iryna Vereshchuk said the last civilians left Azovstal on 7 May 2022.
On 8 May 2022, 173 evacuees reached Zaporizhzhia in 10 buses.
Prokopenko said on 8 May 2022 that fighting was going on inside parts of Azovstal.
US officials said on 9 May 2022 that 2 Russian BTGs remained in Mariupol and more than a dozen had moved to Donbas.

observations.subject: Russian BTGs moved from Mariupol to Donbas

text: Azov chief of staff Bohdan Krotevych asked on 9 May 2022 for a Ukrainian offensive towards the Azovstal defenders.
Dmytro Kozatskyi's photos from inside Azovstal were released on 10 May 2022.
US officials said on 10 May 2022 that Russia was relying on "dumb bombs" at Mariupol.
Azov reported 38 Russian air strikes and 4 strategic-bomber flights against Azovstal in 24 hours on 11 May 2022.
Oleksii Hromov said on 11 May 2022 that unblocking Mariupol was impossible, with Ukrainian units 150–200 km away.

observations.subject: distance from Ukrainian units to Mariupol

text: On 12 May 2022 a Turkish offer to ship the Azovstal defenders out from Berdiansk was made public; Russia refused.
Russian forces blocked the Azovstal tunnel exits on 12 May 2022.
Russian forces secured the M14 highway at Azovstal's western entrance on 13 May 2022.
Thermite incendiaries and naval and air strikes against Azovstal were reported on 14–15 May 2022.
On the evening of 15 May 2022 Serbov was wounded between the ore pile and the rail tracks at Azovstal.
On 16 May 2022 the Ukrainian General Staff declared the Mariupol garrison's mission fulfilled and ordered the commanders to save their men's lives.

text: On 16 May 2022, 53 severely wounded Azovstal defenders were taken to Novoazovsk and 211 to Olenivka.

text: Zelensky said on 16 May 2022: "Ukraine needs Ukrainian heroes alive".
The Russian MoD said on 17 May 2022 that 256 Azovstal defenders, including 51 wounded, had been taken to Olenivka.
Vyacheslav Volodin demanded on 17 May 2022 that the Azovstal defenders face war-crimes trials.
The Russian MoD said on 18 May 2022 that 959 defenders had left Azovstal since 16 May, 694 of them overnight.

observations.subject: defenders out of Azovstal since 16 May

text: Denis Pushilin said on 18 May 2022 that Azovstal would be levelled.
Dmytro Kozatskyi posted his last photos from Azovstal before captivity on 20 May 2022.
Prokopenko announced on 20 May 2022 the order to "stop defending the city".
The Russian MoD said on 20 May 2022 that 2,439 defenders had left Azovstal in total, and Shoigu reported this to Putin.
The Russian MoD claimed full control of Mariupol on 20–21 May 2022.
Seriously wounded Azovstal defenders, including Serbov, were exchanged on 29 June 2022.
On the night of 28–29 July 2022 the Olenivka barracks blast killed at least 50 POWs, according to the UN, many of them from Azovstal.
On 21 September 2022, 215 Ukrainians, including 108 Azov fighters, were freed; five commanders went to Turkey in exchange for Viktor Medvedchuk and 55 Russians.
On 8 July 2023 Zelensky brought the five Azovstal commanders home from Turkey.
A UN report of 4–5 October 2023 found that the Olenivka explosion was not a HIMARS strike.
Andriy Yusov said in May 2025 that 1,279 Azovstal defenders had returned from captivity, 455 of them Azov.

text: Azovstal was founded in 1930.
Azovstal is a full-cycle steel works with coke ovens, a sinter plant, six blast furnaces and a steelmaking complex.
Azovstal's reported size is about 11 km² (ABC) or 4 sq mi, about 10.4 km² (NPR).
The OSM outline of Azovstal measures about 10.3 km² and spans about 6.1 km north–south by 4.8 km east–west.
Azovstal lies on the coast in Mariupol's Left-Bank district, across the river from downtown.
The M14 highway runs past Azovstal's western entrance.
Before the war Azovstal employed more than 10,000 people.
Azovstal has about 24 km of tunnels, built after WWII, with maps posted in each workshop.

metric_new.label: Length of tunnels or underground passages

text: Metinvest said the Azovstal shelters could hold 4,000 people and had food stocks, ventilation, lighting, water and heat-resistant doors.
The Azovstal shelters were stocked for about three weeks.
Evacuees called the Azovstal tunnels a dark maze "like a big city".
The Azovstal defenders moved, shot and communicated through the tunnels, and GAZ-66 trucks brought the wounded up from the tunnels to the helicopters.
At Azovstal tall stacks poked through the fog, power lines 30–40 m high stood on the sea approach, and vertical obstacles stood throughout the compound.

observations.subject: height of power lines on the sea approach

text: A giant ore pile and rail tracks lay inside the Azovstal compound.
Oleksii Hromov put Ukrainian units 150–200 km from Mariupol on 11 May 2022.
The air-bridge helicopters flew about 60 mi (about 97 km) over Russian-held territory after refuelling "right up on the line".
Andriy Biletskyi said the distance to Mariupol over occupied ground was "more than 100 kilometers".
In March 2022 ISW reported up to 17 Russian BTGs assembled as far as Rozivka, about 47 km northwest of Mariupol.

text: The Azov Regiment of the National Guard was commanded by Lt Col Denys Prokopenko "Redis" (born 1991).
Capt Sviatoslav Palamar "Kalyna" was deputy commander of the Azov Regiment at Mariupol.
Maj Bohdan Krotevych was chief of staff of the Azov Regiment at Mariupol.
The Azov Regiment was the core of the Azovstal defence; it lost its Mariupol headquarters on 28 March 2022.
The 36th Marine Brigade (Navy), including the 501st and 503rd battalions, was commanded at Mariupol by Col Volodymyr Baraniuk, captured in the breakout, and then by Maj Serhii Volynskyi "Volyna".
The 36th Marine Brigade held the Illich works, and about 500 of its marines broke through to Azovstal on 12 April 2022.

The National Guard's 12th Operational Brigade, 15th Operational Brigade and 23rd Public Order Protection Brigade were part of the Mariupol garrison; their commanders are not given in the sources fetched.
Russian-led forces entered the base of the 12th Operational Brigade of the National Guard in Mariupol on 16 April 2022.
Elements of the 17th Tank Brigade, the State Border Guard, the National Police and territorial defence were part of the Mariupol garrison.

The Mariupol air bridge flew 7 missions with 16 sorties.
The five "unit leaders of the defence of Azovstal" freed on 21 September 2022 were Denys Prokopenko, Serhii Volynskyi, Sviatoslav Palamar, Denys Shleha and Oleh Khomenko.

text: The Mariupol garrison numbered about 3,500 in March 2022, a Ukrainian estimate quoted by The Economist on 21 March.
Wikipedia extrapolates the Mariupol garrison to up to 4,400 in March 2022.
Russia claimed the Mariupol garrison numbered 8,000 or more in March 2022.
Pro-Russian sources claimed on 8 April 2022 that 3,000 Ukrainian troops were in Azovstal.
A Russian estimate of 18 April 2022 put 2,500 Ukrainian troops plus 400 foreigners at Azovstal.
An outside expert said on 18 April 2022 that 500–800 Ukrainian holdouts remained city-wide in Mariupol.
About 2,000 fighters and up to 1,000 civilians were in Azovstal on 23 April 2022.
Additions to the Azovstal garrison were about 500 marines from Illich, about 500 border guards and police from the port (claimed), and 72 Azov volunteers flown in.

text: There were more than 600 wounded at Azovstal on 27 April 2022.
Before the walk-out, "about 600" wounded at Azovstal had almost no medicine, water or food.
About 2,500 Azovstal defenders were captured at the end of the defence.
The Azovstal defenders were equipped with small arms, Stingers, Starlink and NLAWs delivered by air, which they learned to use from the internet.
Wikipedia lists Javelins on the first air-bridge flight to Azovstal.
A British volunteer said lack of ammunition and supplies was why the marines surrendered at Illich on 12 April 2022.
The 8th Combined Arms Army, commanded by Lt Gen Andrei Mordvichev, fought at Mariupol and included the 150th Motor Rifle Division with the 68th Tank Regiment and 102nd Motor Rifle Regiment.
Black Sea Fleet units at Mariupol included the 810th Naval Infantry Brigade and the 382nd Marine Battalion.
The 810th Naval Infantry Brigade was still blockading Azovstal on 30 April 2022.
Russian Spetsnaz at Mariupol included the 22nd and 346th brigades.
Chechen forces at Mariupol included the 141st Special Motorized Regiment and a Rosgvardia special-purpose police regiment.
DNR 1st Army Corps units at Mariupol included the Vostok Battalion, the "Somalia" tank battalion, the 9th Marine Regiment, the Slovyansk Brigade, the 107th Regiment and Kaskad.
Wikipedia names Mikhail Mizintsev as the overall commander of the Russian siege of Mariupol.
Russian forces at Mariupol numbered about 14,000 in March 2022.

Russian Tu-22M3 bombers struck Azovstal from about 16 April 2022.
Ukraine claims 6,500 Russian troops were killed at Mariupol.
Russian strikes on Mariupol's water, power and heat were meant to force the city's capitulation without an assault.

text: Russia bombed Azovstal heavily with Tu-22M3s.
Multi-ton "bunker-buster" bombs were dropped on the Azovstal field hospital.
Russia flew 38 strikes and 4 bomber flights against Azovstal in a single day.
Russia used unguided "dumb bombs" against Azovstal.
Telegram photos showed a FAB-3000 at a Tu-22M on 6 April 2022, and Ukraine warned of its use on 16 April; use against Azovstal is reported but not confirmed in the sources fetched.
Russian forces at Mariupol used thermobaric weapons.
Russian naval gunfire was used against Azovstal.
Russian forces used thermite incendiaries against Azovstal.
Russian forces used ATGMs against vehicles and people at Azovstal.
Shelters and tunnels let the Azovstal garrison survive bombardment and shift between positions.
Russia answered the Azovstal underground defence by blockading the tunnel exits rather than clearing them.
Russian forces assaulted Azovstal from the north and later along the M14 at the western entrance.
Air-bridge Mi-8s flew nap-of-the-earth at 10–15 m under night-vision goggles, at 3 m in places.
Air-bridge Mi-8s flew at about 150 mph (220 km/h).
Each air-bridge flight took about 80 minutes each way, 42 of them over enemy ground.

text: The air-bridge Mi-8s used a refuelling point at the line on the way back and carried fuel only to that point, to save weight.
Ukrainian artillery fired a distraction at the planned front-line crossing point of the air-bridge flights.
Air-bridge Mi-8s spent 10 minutes on the ground at Azovstal with engines running; two accounts give 12 and 15–20 minutes.

text: Each air-bridge helicopter carried an intelligence officer, and crews wore civilian clothes so they could escape on foot if shot down.
Air-bridge routes alternated between land and sea, once passing between two Russian ships.
Threats to the air bridge were Pantsir-S1 (briefed; no Buk), ship fire, a missile that failed to explode, and MANPADS.
Ukrainian counters on the air bridge were a Mi-24 decoy (which failed on mission 6), surprise, and never sending the same pilot twice.
Russia thickened its air defences once the air-bridge flights became public, which ended the missions.
With no internet, the Azovstal defenders printed A4 leaflets with front news to keep up morale.
Outbound media from Azovstal, such as GoPro clips and Kozatskyi's photos, mattered politically.

rationale: The air-bridge Mi-8s countered the Russian air-defence threat by low flight, surprise, a Mi-24 decoy and rotating pilots.

text: The Mariupol drama theatre, sheltering hundreds, with "children" painted on the square, was hit by two 500 kg bombs shortly after 10:00 on 16 March 2022.
The death toll of the Mariupol theatre strike is contested: at least a dozen (Amnesty), at least 15 (HRW), about 300 (Ukrainian officials) and about 600 (an AP investigation).
The first air-bridge mission had been scrubbed on 19 March 2022, and men in Azovstal had phoned home to say it was off.

On 21 March 2022 two Mi-8s lifted off from Dnipro at 03:30, refuelled at the line, crossed 60 mi of occupied ground at treetop height (one clipped a tree), landed beside a tunnel mouth at Azovstal under Azov covering fire, took on about 16 wounded and were back by 07:30.
One pilot on the first air-bridge mission volunteered because his wife was a combat medic in Azovstal.
On air-bridge mission 3 on 28 March 2022 the guns were stripped for 200 kg more medicine, and the crew was told the flight was "two missions with one helicopter each".

cites.quote: two missions with one helicopter each

text: On mission 3 on 28 March 2022 the pilot found Azovstal by its stacks through the fog at dawn over the sea, popped up over the 30–40 m power lines, dived in and spent 12 minutes on the ground.

text: On the night of 11–12 April 2022 the marines' pocket in the northern Illich works was out of ammunition; two groups broke out, one north under Baraniuk (captured) and one to Azovstal under Volynskyi with about 500 men.
Russia paraded its claimed "1,026 prisoners" from the Illich breakout.
In the staged Putin–Shoigu meeting of 21 April 2022 the storm of Azovstal was called off in favour of starvation.
Heavy bombs hit the Azovstal field hospital on 28 April 2022.
Inside Azovstal amputations were done without painkillers and infections turned deadly.
A UN/ICRC convoy drove 230 km to Azovstal between 29 April and 3 May 2022 and civilians climbed out of the bunkers.
Russian firing on Azovstal resumed the moment the evacuation pause ended in May 2022.
Kozatskyi's photos of Azovstal bunkers and the wounded, including his own portrait in a shaft of light, went out from inside the plant on 10 and 20 May 2022.
Kozatskyi's last post before captivity read: "I am thankful to Azovstal for shelter – the place of my death and my life".

cites.quote: I am thankful to Azovstal for shelter – the place of my death and my life

text: Before leaving Azovstal in May 2022 the defenders destroyed phones, weapons and documents.
In the walk-out of 16–20 May 2022 the wounded went to Novoazovsk and the rest of the defenders to Olenivka.
The Olenivka barracks explosion of 28–29 July 2022 killed at least 50 prisoners.
The UN later ruled out a HIMARS strike as the cause of the Olenivka explosion.
In March 2022 Budanov (HUR) devised the Mariupol air-bridge plan, which a US aviation veteran called work for highly proficient crews only.
Several Ukrainian pilots opted out of the Mariupol air bridge once they were read in.
Each air-bridge flight needed the final "all clear" from the Azovstal ground commander, Prokopenko.
After the seventh mission HUR judged further air-bridge flights to Azovstal too risky.
Hromov said air-bridge deliveries stopped once news of them spread and Russia strengthened its air defences.

Air-bridge crews faced real dilemmas: payload against defensive guns (the guns were removed), re-routing around updated air-defence positions while keeping the supporting artillery in sync, extra minutes on the ground to load every wounded man at a cost in fuel, and the "single-ship mission" rule under which no one turned back to save a downed partner.
At Illich on 11–12 April 2022 the 36th Marine Brigade split: one group went north to break the ring and the other went to link up with Azov.
Prokopenko later called Baraniuk's breakout from Illich "uncoordinated".
ISW and Ukrainian officials confirmed that the 36th Marine Brigade's link-up with Azov partly succeeded.
On 21 April 2022 Putin halted the assaults on Azovstal to limit casualties, choosing to starve rather than storm the plant.
Russian ground attacks on Azovstal resumed on 25 April 2022 and became a full storm on 3–4 May, which ISW linked to the 9 May Victory Day deadline.
The UN/ICRC safe passage from Azovstal was agreed after Guterres visited Moscow and Kyiv in late April 2022.
Russia first refused any humanitarian pause at Azovstal until the defenders surrendered.
The Azovstal defenders asked for a Ukrainian offensive towards them.
Hromov and Maliar ruled out unblocking Mariupol, citing 150–200 km of fortified ground and heavy losses.

observations.subject: fortified ground between Ukrainian lines and Mariupol

text: Volynskyi appealed to world leaders for a "Dunkirk" extraction of the Azovstal defenders.
Turkey offered to carry the Azovstal defenders by ship from Berdiansk and intern them until the war's end; Russia would release only civilians.
Ukraine separately proposed swapping the seriously wounded Azovstal defenders for Russian prisoners.
No source examined describes a planned breakout from Azovstal itself.
notes: the block cites isw-2022-05-06-roca only for the escapee claim; cited here as background

text: Russian claims of captured Azovstal "escapees" on 6 May 2022 are unconfirmed.
On 16 May 2022 the Supreme Military Command ordered the Mariupol unit commanders to save their men.
Ukraine framed the 16 May 2022 Azovstal walk-out as an "evacuation" with later exchange, while Russia called it a surrender.
ISW judged that the Kremlin might have agreed to a conditional Azovstal surrender to speed up its claim of control, and warned that it might refuse exchanges.
The five Azovstal commanders freed in September 2022 were released on condition that they stay in Turkey under Erdoğan's guarantees.
The five Azovstal commanders returned to Ukraine with Zelensky on 8 July 2023.
The slow return of Azov fighters from captivity remained contested in 2025; Prokopenko called a swap without Azov fighters "a disgrace".
Putin and Shoigu declared victory in Mariupol on 21 April 2022 while Azovstal still held; Putin framed the halt to assaults as a way to limit Russian casualties.
ISW read the Kremlin as setting up a claim of control over Mariupol by 9 May 2022, with propagandists brought into the city.
Shoigu claimed more than 8,000 Ukrainian troops were in Mariupol at the time of encirclement.
Shoigu claimed 1,026 marines surrendered at Illich.
Shoigu claimed 2,439 Ukrainian defenders surrendered at Azovstal.
ISW suggested Russia might overstate its Azovstal prisoner totals, either to maximise exchange leverage or to avoid admitting a months-long siege against only "hundreds".
Russia presented civilians evacuated from Azovstal as freed "hostages".
Russia said a downed Ukrainian helicopter had been sent to evacuate Azov commanders from Mariupol.
Vyacheslav Volodin said the Azovstal defenders must be tried for war crimes and not exchanged.
Pro-Russian channels were angry about the negotiated Azovstal deal in May 2022.
Pro-Russian channels complained that Russian wounded were moved out of DNR hospitals to make room for wounded Ukrainians from Azovstal.
Denis Pushilin announced that Azovstal would be demolished and Mariupol made a "resort city".
Russia blamed the Olenivka explosion on HIMARS, which the UN rejected.
Russian courts sentenced 12 Azov members to 13–23 years in March 2025.
Andrei Paly, deputy commander of the Black Sea Fleet, was confirmed killed at Mariupol.
A Ukrainian claim names the 150th Motor Rifle Division commander, Maj Gen Mityaev, as killed at Mariupol.
